title: The Specific Relief Act, 1877 (Bangladesh) - BJSC MCQ Bank - Batch 1
note: This is Batch 1 of 3, containing 100 MCQs out of a planned 300-question BJSC-oriented bank. Questions are based on the Specific Relief Act, 1877 as applicable in Bangladesh, including important amendments. Section 21A was inserted by the Specific Relief (Amendment) Act, 2004 with effect from 1 July 2005. The questions emphasize statutory provisions, section numbers, exceptions, illustrations, and commonly testable distinctions. Cross-check the latest Bangladesh Code/bare Act before the examination.

mcqs.question: The Specific Relief Act, 1877 is:
mcqs.answer: Act No. I of 1877

mcqs.question: The Specific Relief Act, 1877 extends to:
options: Only the territorial areas of Dhaka and Chattogram
Only immovable property situated in Bangladesh
mcqs.answer: The whole of Bangladesh

mcqs.question: The Specific Relief Act, 1877 came into force on:
Section 2 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 is:
options: The provision relating to specific performance
mcqs.answer: Repealed

mcqs.question: Under section 3, 'obligation' includes:
mcqs.answer: Every duty enforceable by law

mcqs.question: Under section 3, 'trust' includes:
options: Every species of express, implied, or constructive fiduciary ownership
mcqs.answer: Every species of express, implied, or constructive fiduciary ownership

mcqs.question: Under section 3, a 'trustee' includes:
options: Every person holding expressly, by implication, or constructively, a fiduciary character
Only a person appointed by a court
Only a person appointed under the Trusts Act
mcqs.answer: Every person holding expressly, by implication, or constructively, a fiduciary character

mcqs.question: Specific relief may be given by taking possession of certain property and:
mcqs.answer: Delivering it to a claimant

mcqs.question: Specific relief under section 5 may be given by ordering a party:
options: To do the very act which he is under an obligation to do
mcqs.answer: To do the very act which he is under an obligation to do

mcqs.question: Specific relief may be given by preventing a party from doing that which he is under an obligation:
mcqs.answer: Not to do

mcqs.question: Which of the following is expressly mentioned in section 5 as a mode of giving specific relief?
mcqs.answer: Appointing a receiver

mcqs.question: Specific relief granted under section 5(c) is called:
mcqs.answer: Preventive relief

mcqs.question: Specific relief cannot be granted for the mere purpose of:
mcqs.answer: Enforcing a penal law

mcqs.question: A person entitled to possession of specific immovable property may recover it in the manner prescribed by:
mcqs.answer: The Code of Civil Procedure

mcqs.question: Section 9 applies where a person is dispossessed of immovable property:
options: Without his consent otherwise than in due course of law
mcqs.answer: Without his consent otherwise than in due course of law

mcqs.question: In a suit under section 9, the defendant may set up:
options: Any other title as a defence, but that does not prevent the statutory remedy
Only a title obtained after dispossession
mcqs.answer: Any other title as a defence, but that does not prevent the statutory remedy

mcqs.question: A suit under section 9 does not bar a person from suing to:
options: Establish his title and recover possession
mcqs.answer: Establish his title and recover possession

mcqs.question: A suit under section 9 may be brought against:
options: The Government and no private person
Only a trespasser who admits possession
mcqs.answer: Any person except the Government

mcqs.question: From an order or decree passed in a suit under section 9:
options: An appeal lies only with Government permission
mcqs.answer: No appeal lies

mcqs.question: Under section 9, review of an order or decree passed in such a suit is:
mcqs.answer: Not allowed

mcqs.question: A person entitled to possession of specific movable property may recover it in the manner prescribed by:
mcqs.answer: The Code of Civil Procedure

mcqs.question: Under section 10, a trustee may sue for possession of movable property for:
options: The beneficial interest to which the person for whom he is trustee is entitled
mcqs.answer: The beneficial interest to which the person for whom he is trustee is entitled

mcqs.question: Under section 10, a special or temporary right to present possession of property is:
mcqs.answer: Sufficient to support a suit

mcqs.question: Section 11 concerns a person having possession or control of a particular article of movable property who is:
mcqs.answer: Not the owner

mcqs.question: Under section 11, specific delivery may be compelled where the thing claimed is held by the defendant as:
options: Agent or trustee of the claimant
mcqs.answer: Agent or trustee of the claimant

mcqs.question: Under section 11, specific delivery may be ordered where compensation in money would:
options: Be greater than the value of the property
mcqs.answer: Not afford adequate relief

mcqs.question: Specific performance under section 12 may be enforced:
options: In the discretion of the Court
Only by consent of the defendant
mcqs.answer: In the discretion of the Court

mcqs.question: Specific performance may be granted where the act agreed to be done is wholly or partly in the performance of:
mcqs.answer: A trust

mcqs.question: Specific performance may be granted where there exists no standard for ascertaining:
options: The actual damage caused by non-performance
mcqs.answer: The actual damage caused by non-performance

mcqs.question: Specific performance may be granted when pecuniary compensation for non-performance would:
options: Be unnecessary because there was no contract
mcqs.answer: Not afford adequate relief

mcqs.question: Under section 12, in the absence of proof to the contrary, breach of a contract to transfer immovable property is presumed to be:
options: Not adequately relieved by compensation in money
mcqs.answer: Not adequately relieved by compensation in money

mcqs.question: Under section 12, breach of a contract to transfer movable property is presumed, unless the contrary is proved, to be:
options: Adequately relieved by compensation in money
mcqs.answer: Adequately relieved by compensation in money

mcqs.question: If the Court refuses specific performance but finds a valid contract broken by the defendant and the plaintiff entitled to compensation, the Court:
options: Must dismiss the suit without compensation
Must refer the matter to arbitration
mcqs.answer: Shall award compensation

mcqs.question: Section 13 deals with a contract whose subject-matter has:
mcqs.answer: Partially ceased to exist

mcqs.question: A contract is not wholly impossible of performance merely because:
options: A portion of its subject-matter existing at its date has ceased to exist at the time of performance
mcqs.answer: A portion of its subject-matter existing at its date has ceased to exist at the time of performance

mcqs.question: Under section 14, where the unperformed part is only a small proportion of the whole in value and admits of compensation in money, the Court may:
options: Order specific performance of the performable part and award compensation for the deficiency
mcqs.answer: Order specific performance of the performable part and award compensation for the deficiency

mcqs.question: Where the unperformed part forms a considerable portion of the whole, the party unable to perform the whole is generally:
options: Not entitled to obtain a decree for specific performance
Entitled to specific performance without conditions
mcqs.answer: Not entitled to obtain a decree for specific performance

mcqs.question: Under section 15, the Court may direct the party in default to perform specifically so much as he can perform if the other party:
options: Relinquishes all claim to further performance and compensation for the deficiency or loss
Refuses to perform his own part
mcqs.answer: Relinquishes all claim to further performance and compensation for the deficiency or loss

mcqs.question: Section 16 permits specific performance of a part of a contract when that part:
options: Can and ought to be specifically performed and stands on a separate and independent footing
mcqs.answer: Can and ought to be specifically performed and stands on a separate and independent footing

mcqs.question: Section 17 generally provides that the Court shall not direct specific performance of part of a contract except in cases falling under:
mcqs.answer: Sections 14, 15 or 16

mcqs.question: A person suing for specific performance may also ask for compensation:
options: In addition to or in substitution for specific performance
Only after execution of the decree
mcqs.answer: In addition to or in substitution for specific performance

mcqs.question: Under section 19, compensation may be awarded even where the contract has become:
mcqs.answer: Incapable of specific performance

mcqs.question: A contract otherwise proper to be specifically enforced may be specifically enforced even though:
options: A sum is named as the amount to be paid in case of breach
The defendant has already paid damages
The plaintiff has no legal right
mcqs.answer: A sum is named as the amount to be paid in case of breach

mcqs.question: A contract cannot be specifically enforced where compensation in money is:
options: An adequate relief for its non-performance
mcqs.answer: An adequate relief for its non-performance

mcqs.question: A contract depending on personal qualifications or volition of the parties may be incapable of specific enforcement where:
options: The Court cannot enforce its material terms
mcqs.answer: The Court cannot enforce its material terms

mcqs.question: A contract whose terms cannot be found with reasonable certainty:
options: Can be enforced only against the Government
mcqs.answer: Cannot be specifically enforced

mcqs.question: A contract which is in its nature revocable:
options: Can only be enforced against a stranger
mcqs.answer: Cannot be specifically enforced

mcqs.question: A contract made by trustees in excess of their powers or in breach of their trust:
options: Is enforceable only by the Government
mcqs.answer: Cannot be specifically enforced

mcqs.question: A contract made by or on behalf of a corporation created for special purposes, when it is in excess of its powers:
mcqs.answer: Cannot be specifically enforced

mcqs.question: Under section 21A, a contract for sale of immovable property cannot be specifically enforced unless the contract is:
options: In writing and registered under the Registration Act, 1908
Registered only after filing the suit
mcqs.answer: In writing and registered under the Registration Act, 1908

mcqs.question: Under section 21A, for specific performance of a contract for sale of immovable property, the balance amount of consideration must be:
options: Deposited in court at the time of filing the suit
Paid to the defendant before filing the suit
mcqs.answer: Deposited in court at the time of filing the suit

mcqs.question: Section 21A was inserted by:
mcqs.answer: The Specific Relief (Amendment) Act, 2004
mcqs.reference: Specific Relief Act, 1877, S.21A amendment note

mcqs.question: Section 21A came into effect on:
mcqs.answer: 1 July 2005
mcqs.reference: Specific Relief Act, 1877, amendment note to S.21A

mcqs.question: The jurisdiction to decree specific performance is:
mcqs.answer: Discretionary

mcqs.question: The discretion under section 22 is not arbitrary but must be:
options: Sound and reasonable, guided by judicial principles
Based solely on the defendant's wishes
mcqs.answer: Sound and reasonable, guided by judicial principles

mcqs.question: The discretion of the Court under section 22 is capable of correction by:
mcqs.answer: A Court of appeal

mcqs.topic: Who May Obtain Specific Performance - S.23
mcqs.question: Under section 23, specific performance may generally be obtained by:
mcqs.answer: Any party to the contract

mcqs.topic: Who May Obtain Specific Performance - S.23
mcqs.question: A representative in interest may generally obtain specific performance subject to the exceptions concerning:
mcqs.answer: Personal qualities and non-assignment

mcqs.topic: Who May Obtain Specific Performance - S.23
mcqs.question: Where a contract is a settlement on marriage, a person who may obtain specific performance includes:
options: Any person beneficially entitled under the settlement
mcqs.answer: Any person beneficially entitled under the settlement

mcqs.topic: Who May Obtain Specific Performance - S.23
mcqs.question: Where a contract is a compromise of doubtful rights between members of the same family, who may obtain specific performance?
mcqs.answer: A person beneficially entitled thereunder

mcqs.topic: Who May Obtain Specific Performance - S.23
mcqs.question: A remainderman may obtain specific performance where the contract has been entered into by:
options: A tenant for life in due exercise of a power
mcqs.answer: A tenant for life in due exercise of a power

mcqs.topic: Who May Obtain Specific Performance - S.23
mcqs.question: A reversioner in possession may obtain specific performance where the agreement is a covenant entered into with:
mcqs.answer: His predecessor in title

mcqs.topic: Who May Obtain Specific Performance - S.23
mcqs.question: A reversioner in remainder may obtain specific performance where breach would cause:
mcqs.answer: Material injury

mcqs.topic: Who May Obtain Specific Performance - S.23
mcqs.question: Where a public company becomes amalgamated with another public company, a contract entered into by the original company may be specifically enforced by:
options: The new company arising from the amalgamation
mcqs.answer: The new company arising from the amalgamation

mcqs.topic: Who May Obtain Specific Performance - S.23
mcqs.question: A company may enforce a pre-incorporation contract entered into by its promoters when the contract is:
options: For the purposes of the company and warranted by the terms of incorporation
For any personal purpose of the promoter
mcqs.answer: For the purposes of the company and warranted by the terms of incorporation

mcqs.question: Specific performance cannot be enforced in favour of a person who:
options: Could not recover compensation for the breach
Is a party to the contract
mcqs.answer: Could not recover compensation for the breach

mcqs.question: Section 24 is concerned with:
mcqs.answer: Personal bars to specific performance

mcqs.question: Section 26 deals with:
mcqs.answer: Non-enforcement except with variation

mcqs.question: Under section 26, specific performance may be refused except with a variation where fraud or mistake of fact caused the contract sought to be enforced to differ from:
options: The contract the defendant supposed it to be
The contract registered by the Government
mcqs.answer: The contract the defendant supposed it to be

mcqs.question: Specific performance may generally be enforced against:
mcqs.answer: Either party to the contract

mcqs.question: A subsequent transferee for value who has paid his money in good faith and without notice of the original contract is generally:
options: Protected from specific performance under section 27
mcqs.answer: Protected from specific performance under section 27

mcqs.question: Specific performance cannot be enforced against a party where the consideration to be received by him is so grossly inadequate as to be evidence of:
options: Fraud or undue advantage taken by the plaintiff
mcqs.answer: Fraud or undue advantage taken by the plaintiff

mcqs.question: Specific performance cannot be enforced against a party whose assent was obtained by:
options: Misrepresentation, concealment, circumvention or unfair practices
mcqs.answer: Misrepresentation, concealment, circumvention or unfair practices

mcqs.question: Under section 28, assent given under the influence of mistake of fact, misapprehension or surprise may constitute:
options: A bar to specific performance against the party
mcqs.answer: A bar to specific performance against the party

mcqs.question: Dismissal of a suit for specific performance of a contract bars the plaintiff's subsequent right to sue for:
options: Compensation for the breach of that contract
mcqs.answer: Compensation for the breach of that contract

mcqs.question: The provisions of Chapter II as to contracts apply, mutatis mutandis, to:
options: Awards and directions in a will or codicil to execute a particular settlement
mcqs.answer: Awards and directions in a will or codicil to execute a particular settlement

mcqs.question: An instrument may be rectified where, through fraud or mutual mistake, it does not:
options: Truly express the intention of the parties
mcqs.answer: Truly express the intention of the parties

mcqs.question: Who may institute a suit for rectification under section 31?
options: Either party or his representative in interest
mcqs.answer: Either party or his representative in interest

mcqs.question: Rectification cannot prejudice rights acquired by third persons:
options: In good faith and for value
Without consideration and in bad faith
mcqs.answer: In good faith and for value

mcqs.question: For rectifying a written contract, the Court must be satisfied that all parties intended to make:
mcqs.answer: An equitable and conscientious agreement

mcqs.question: In rectifying a written instrument, the Court may inquire into:
options: What the instrument was intended to mean and its intended legal consequences
Only the literal dictionary meaning of every word
Only the market value of the property
Only the intention of the defendant
mcqs.answer: What the instrument was intended to mean and its intended legal consequences

mcqs.question: A written contract may be first rectified and then specifically enforced if:
options: The plaintiff has so prayed in the plaint and the Court thinks fit
mcqs.answer: The plaintiff has so prayed in the plaint and the Court thinks fit

mcqs.question: Who may sue to have a contract in writing rescinded under section 35?
options: Any person interested in the contract
mcqs.answer: Any person interested in the contract

mcqs.question: A contract may be rescinded under section 35 where it is:
options: Voidable or terminable by the plaintiff
mcqs.answer: Voidable or terminable by the plaintiff

mcqs.question: An unlawful contract may be rescinded under section 35 where the unlawfulness is:
options: For causes not apparent on its face and the defendant is more to blame than the plaintiff
Apparent on its face in every case
mcqs.answer: For causes not apparent on its face and the defendant is more to blame than the plaintiff

mcqs.question: Where a decree for specific performance of a sale contract has been made and the purchaser defaults in payment ordered by the Court, the contract may be:
mcqs.answer: Rescinded

mcqs.question: If a purchaser or lessee is in possession and the Court finds the possession wrongful, the Court may order payment of:
options: Rents and profits received as such possessor
mcqs.answer: Rents and profits received as such possessor

mcqs.question: Rescission for mere mistake cannot generally be adjudged unless the party against whom rescission is ordered can be restored to:
options: Substantially the same position as if the contract had not been made
A position chosen by the plaintiff
A position determined by the police
mcqs.answer: Substantially the same position as if the contract had not been made

mcqs.question: A plaintiff seeking specific performance may pray in the alternative for:
options: Rescission and delivery up of the contract for cancellation
mcqs.answer: Rescission and delivery up of the contract for cancellation

mcqs.question: On adjudging rescission of a contract, the Court may require the party receiving relief to make:
options: Compensation to the other party as justice may require
mcqs.answer: Compensation to the other party as justice may require

mcqs.question: A person against whom a written instrument is void or voidable may sue for cancellation when he has reasonable apprehension that leaving it outstanding may cause:
mcqs.answer: Serious injury

mcqs.question: Cancellation of an instrument under section 39 is:
options: A discretionary relief of the Court
mcqs.answer: A discretionary relief of the Court

mcqs.question: Where an instrument is evidence of different rights or obligations, the Court may:
options: Cancel it in part and allow it to stand for the residue
mcqs.answer: Cancel it in part and allow it to stand for the residue

mcqs.question: On adjudging cancellation of an instrument, the Court may require the party receiving relief to make:
options: Compensation to the other party as justice may require
A new instrument in every case
Payment to the Government in every case
mcqs.answer: Compensation to the other party as justice may require

mcqs.question: A person entitled to any legal character or any right as to property may institute a suit against a person:
options: Denying or interested to deny his title to that character or right
Who is unrelated to the matter
Who is necessarily a Government officer
mcqs.answer: Denying or interested to deny his title to that character or right

mcqs.question: A declaratory decree under section 42 is granted:
options: In the discretion of the Court
mcqs.answer: In the discretion of the Court

mcqs.question: A declaration under Chapter VI is binding upon:
options: The parties to the suit and persons claiming through them respectively
mcqs.answer: The parties to the suit and persons claiming through them respectively

mcqs.question: The appointment of a receiver pending a suit is a matter:
options: Resting in the discretion of the Court
mcqs.answer: Resting in the discretion of the Court

mcqs.question: The mode and effect of appointment of a receiver and his rights, powers, duties and liabilities are regulated by:
mcqs.answer: The Code of Civil Procedure

mcqs.question: Preventive relief is granted by way of:
mcqs.answer: Injunction, temporary or perpetual

mcqs.question: Under section 22, the Court is not bound to grant specific performance merely because:
options: It is lawful to do so
mcqs.answer: It is lawful to do so

mcqs.question: The discretion of the Court under section 22 must be:
options: Sound and reasonable and guided by judicial principles
Based solely on the plaintiff's choice
Based solely on the market price
mcqs.answer: Sound and reasonable and guided by judicial principles

mcqs.question: The discretion exercised under section 22 is capable of correction by:
mcqs.answer: A Court of appeal

mcqs.question: Specific performance may properly be refused where the circumstances of the contract give the plaintiff:
options: An unfair advantage over the defendant
mcqs.answer: An unfair advantage over the defendant

mcqs.question: Under section 22, an unfair advantage may justify refusal of specific performance:
options: Even where there is no fraud or misrepresentation by the plaintiff
Only where criminal conduct is proved
mcqs.answer: Even where there is no fraud or misrepresentation by the plaintiff

mcqs.question: Specific performance may be refused where the contract would involve:
options: Hardship to the defendant which he did not foresee
mcqs.answer: Hardship to the defendant which he did not foresee

mcqs.question: The mere fact that a contract has become:
options: More onerous to the defendant is not by itself sufficient to refuse specific performance
Written is sufficient to refuse specific performance
Registered is sufficient to refuse specific performance
Oral is sufficient to refuse specific performance
mcqs.answer: More onerous to the defendant is not by itself sufficient to refuse specific performance

mcqs.topic: Who May Obtain Specific Performance - S.23
mcqs.question: Specific performance may be obtained by a person claiming under a party to a contract unless:
options: The contract depends upon personal qualifications or is non-assignable
mcqs.answer: The contract depends upon personal qualifications or is non-assignable

mcqs.topic: Who May Obtain Specific Performance - S.23
mcqs.question: A representative in interest may enforce a contract when:
options: The contract is not dependent upon personal qualifications and is otherwise assignable
The original party has repudiated it
mcqs.answer: The contract is not dependent upon personal qualifications and is otherwise assignable

mcqs.topic: Who May Obtain Specific Performance - S.23
mcqs.question: A beneficiary under a marriage settlement may seek:
options: Only a writ of habeas corpus
mcqs.answer: Specific performance

mcqs.topic: Who May Obtain Specific Performance - S.23
mcqs.question: A person beneficially entitled under a compromise of doubtful rights between members of a family may:
mcqs.answer: Obtain specific performance

mcqs.topic: Who May Obtain Specific Performance - S.23
mcqs.question: A remainderman may obtain specific performance of a contract entered into by:
options: A tenant for life in due exercise of a power
mcqs.answer: A tenant for life in due exercise of a power

mcqs.topic: Who May Obtain Specific Performance - S.23
mcqs.question: A reversioner in possession may obtain specific performance of a covenant entered into with:
mcqs.answer: His predecessor in title

mcqs.topic: Who May Obtain Specific Performance - S.23
mcqs.question: A reversioner in remainder must show what additional circumstance when seeking specific performance of a covenant?
options: That he will sustain material injury from its breach
That he is a Government employee
That he has paid stamp duty
mcqs.answer: That he will sustain material injury from its breach

mcqs.question: When a public company amalgamates with another public company, the new company may enforce a contract entered into by:
mcqs.answer: The original company

mcqs.question: A company may enforce a pre-incorporation contract made by its promoters when it was made:
options: For the purposes of the company and warranted by the terms of incorporation
Without any connection to the company
mcqs.answer: For the purposes of the company and warranted by the terms of incorporation

mcqs.question: Specific performance cannot be enforced in favour of a person who:
options: Could not recover compensation for the breach
Is a party to the contract
mcqs.answer: Could not recover compensation for the breach

mcqs.question: A person who has become incapable of performing, or violates, an essential term of the contract on his part may be:
mcqs.answer: Barred from obtaining specific performance

mcqs.question: A plaintiff who has acted in fraud of the contract or wilfully acted at variance with its terms may:
mcqs.answer: Be denied specific performance

mcqs.question: A plaintiff who fails to prove that he has performed or has always been ready and willing to perform the essential terms may:
options: Obtain a perpetual injunction as of right
mcqs.answer: Be barred from specific performance

mcqs.question: Section 25 deals with:
mcqs.answer: Specific performance with a variation

mcqs.question: A written contract may be specifically enforced with a variation where the variation:
options: Does not materially alter the character of the contract
mcqs.answer: Does not materially alter the character of the contract

mcqs.question: Under section 26, fraud or mutual mistake may justify refusal of specific performance when the written contract does not truly express:
mcqs.answer: The intention of the parties

mcqs.question: Where the contract differs from what the defendant supposed it to be because of fraud or mutual mistake, the Court may:
options: Refuse enforcement except with a variation
Always enforce it exactly as written
mcqs.answer: Refuse enforcement except with a variation

mcqs.question: Specific performance may generally be enforced against:
mcqs.answer: Either party to the contract

mcqs.question: A person claiming under a party to the contract may be bound by specific performance unless he is:
options: A transferee for value who paid in good faith and without notice
mcqs.answer: A transferee for value who paid in good faith and without notice

mcqs.question: A subsequent transferee who had notice of the original contract is:
options: Not protected by the bona fide purchaser exception
mcqs.answer: Not protected by the bona fide purchaser exception

mcqs.question: Gross inadequacy of consideration may prevent specific performance when it is evidence of:
mcqs.answer: Fraud or undue advantage

mcqs.question: Under section 28, assent obtained by innocent misrepresentation may:
mcqs.answer: Bar specific performance

mcqs.question: Concealment or circumvention in obtaining assent to a contract may result in:
mcqs.answer: Specific performance being refused

mcqs.question: A promise by the party seeking performance that has not been substantially fulfilled may be relevant to:
options: Refusing specific performance against the other party
mcqs.answer: Refusing specific performance against the other party

mcqs.question: Assent obtained by mistake of fact, misapprehension or surprise may constitute:
mcqs.answer: A bar to specific performance

mcqs.question: Dismissal of a suit for specific performance bars a subsequent suit for:
options: Compensation for breach of that contract
mcqs.answer: Compensation for breach of that contract

mcqs.question: Chapter II provisions relating to contracts apply, mutatis mutandis, to:
mcqs.answer: Awards

mcqs.question: Rectification is available where, through fraud or mutual mistake, an instrument fails to:
options: Express the real intention of the parties
mcqs.answer: Express the real intention of the parties

mcqs.question: A suit for rectification may be instituted by:
options: Either party or his representative in interest
mcqs.answer: Either party or his representative in interest

mcqs.question: Rectification cannot prejudice rights acquired by third persons:
options: In good faith and for value
mcqs.answer: In good faith and for value

mcqs.question: Before rectifying a written contract, the Court must be satisfied that the parties intended to make:
mcqs.answer: An equitable and conscientious agreement

mcqs.question: In rectifying an instrument, the Court may ascertain:
options: The true intention and intended legal consequences
mcqs.answer: The true intention and intended legal consequences

mcqs.question: A plaintiff may seek rectification and specific performance in the same suit when:
options: The plaint contains the appropriate prayer
mcqs.answer: The plaint contains the appropriate prayer

mcqs.question: A person interested in a contract in writing may sue for rescission where the contract is:
mcqs.answer: Voidable or terminable by him

mcqs.question: An unlawful contract may be rescinded where its unlawfulness is:
options: Not apparent on its face and the defendant is more to blame
Apparent on its face in every case
mcqs.answer: Not apparent on its face and the defendant is more to blame

mcqs.question: After a decree for specific performance of a sale contract, failure by the purchaser to pay the purchase-money within the period fixed may lead to:
mcqs.answer: Rescission of the contract

mcqs.question: When a purchaser or lessee is in possession under a contract that is rescinded, the Court may require him to pay:
options: Rents and profits received during wrongful possession
mcqs.answer: Rents and profits received during wrongful possession

mcqs.question: Rescission for mere mistake should generally not be adjudged where the other party cannot be restored to:
options: Substantially the same position as if the contract had not been made
A position selected by the plaintiff
A position selected by the defendant
mcqs.answer: Substantially the same position as if the contract had not been made

mcqs.question: A plaintiff suing for specific performance may include an alternative prayer for:
mcqs.answer: Rescission

mcqs.question: Where a contract has been rescinded, the Court may require the party receiving relief to make:
mcqs.answer: Compensation as justice may require

mcqs.question: A person may seek cancellation of a written instrument when it is:
mcqs.answer: Void or voidable against him

mcqs.question: The plaintiff seeking cancellation must have reasonable apprehension that leaving the instrument outstanding may cause:
mcqs.answer: Serious injury

mcqs.question: When an instrument has been registered, the Court adjudging cancellation must send a copy of its decree to:
options: The officer in whose office the instrument has been registered
mcqs.answer: The officer in whose office the instrument has been registered

mcqs.question: Where an instrument evidences different rights or obligations, the Court may:
options: Cancel it in part and allow the remainder to stand
mcqs.answer: Cancel it in part and allow the remainder to stand

mcqs.question: When cancellation is adjudged, the Court may require the party receiving relief to make:
options: A new deed in every case
mcqs.answer: Compensation as justice may require

mcqs.question: A person entitled to a legal character or right as to property may sue when another person:
options: Denies or is interested to deny that title
mcqs.answer: Denies or is interested to deny that title

mcqs.question: A suit for a declaration under section 42 is:
mcqs.answer: Discretionary

mcqs.question: A plaintiff seeking only a declaration cannot ordinarily obtain it where he is able to seek:
options: Further relief than a mere declaration but omits to do so
mcqs.answer: Further relief than a mere declaration but omits to do so

mcqs.question: The proviso to section 42 is primarily intended to prevent:
options: A plaintiff from seeking a bare declaration when further relief is available but omitted
mcqs.answer: A plaintiff from seeking a bare declaration when further relief is available but omitted

mcqs.question: A declaration under Chapter VI is binding upon:
options: The parties to the suit and persons claiming through them
mcqs.answer: The parties to the suit and persons claiming through them

mcqs.question: Appointment of a receiver pending a suit is:
